item.title: Overcoming the Spin Barrier of Oxygen Redox Chemistry in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries via Metal–Support Magnetic Interaction
item.description:

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Metal–support magnetic interaction is used to overcome the spin barrier in Li–O₂ batteries. Interfacial magnetic coupling between Pd and ferrimagnetic CoFe₂O₄ restructures Pd spin states, promoting triplet O₂ conversion to peroxide while suppressing singlet O₂. This yields a 0.05 V charging overpotential and 91.2% energy efficiency, establishing a general design principle for spin-dependent oxygen electrocatalysis.

item.title: Improving the Calendar Life of Silicon Anodes with Inorganic Solid–Electrolyte Interphases
item.description:

ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This study uniquely contrasts calendar aging in single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes versus carbonate electrolytes, showing mixed-salt LSCEs form predominantly inorganic SEIs that dramatically extend silicon anode calendar life (96% vs. 77% capacity after one month). It identifies SEI reinforcement via controlled anion/solvent redox as a key strategy, offering significant guidance for durable high-energy silicon anode batteries.

item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using Bi₁₂.₆₇S₁₈Br₂ nanorods with iodide additive to create successive redox mediation via gradient-potential couples (I⁰/I⁻ > Bi³⁺/Bi⁰ > S⁰/S²⁻), accelerating sulfur kinetics and suppressing side reactions. This enables high-capacity aqueous Zn–S batteries (792 mAh g⁻¹, 488.2 Wh kg⁻¹) with practical pouch-cell cycling, offering a new design principle for energy storage.

item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a matched polymer–electrolyte co-solvation state within a dual-regulated gel polymer electrolyte, combining a fluorinated backbone, amide crosslinker, and weakly solvating adiponitrile. This enables cooperative Li+ hopping and vehicular diffusion while suppressing anion migration, achieving 10,000 cycles at 6 C with 0.003% decay per cycle. It establishes co-solvation as a design framework for fast-charging lithium metal batteries.

item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work decouples bulk solvation from interfacial adsorption by showing that proline amide enantiomers, despite identical solvation energetics, behave differently at the Zn interface. Chirality governs adsorption geometry, with L-proline amide enabling dendrite-free deposition, 2500 h cycling, and 99.39% Coulombic efficiency, establishing molecular stereostructure as a design descriptor for aqueous zinc battery electrolytes.
